Cleaning fossil records

Source: vignettes/fossils.Rmd
fossils.Rmd

Fossil occurrences, such as those downloaded from the Paleobiology Database (PBDB), carry the same coordinate errors as modern records and one more field to check: the age of the record, given as a stratigraphic range from a minimum to a maximum age in million years (Ma). This article flags a fossil table with the coordinate tests and the age test age_equal, keeps the width of the age range as a raw column to cut at tally time, and shows how fossil specimens are separated in GBIF data.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/OccurrenceCleaner")

Needs a C++ compiler (Rtools on Windows).

library(OccurrenceCleaner)

Example data

A PBDB download holds the taxon in accepted_name, coordinates in lng and lat, the country as an alpha-2 code in cc, and the age range in min_ma and max_ma. The simulated table has 1,500 Paleogene mammal occurrences from the interior of the western United States, Mongolia and Germany, with age ranges between 1 and 12 Ma:

set.seed(5)
n <- 1500
region <- sample(c("US", "MN", "DE"), n, TRUE, prob = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2))
box <- list(US = c(-112, -104, 38, 46), MN = c(98, 110, 43, 47), DE = c(7, 13, 49, 52))
b <- t(sapply(region, function(r) box[[r]]))
min_ma <- round(runif(n, 23, 60), 1)
fos <- data.frame(
  occurrence_no = seq_len(n),
  accepted_name = sample(c("Hyracotherium", "Coryphodon", "Mesonyx", "Uintatherium", "Andrewsarchus"), n, TRUE),
  lng = round(runif(n, b[, 1], b[, 2]), 3),
  lat = round(runif(n, b[, 3], b[, 4]), 3),
  cc = region,
  min_ma = min_ma,
  max_ma = min_ma + round(runif(n, 1, 12), 1),
  truth = "clean")

Into it go the errors that the fossil tests target. Collections georeferenced to the centroid of their country, or roughly 3 km from it, specimens placed at the museum that holds them (the Senckenberg museum in Frankfurt, the Natural History Museum in London), zero coordinates, records whose minimum age was copied into the maximum or the two swapped, and records dated only to a whole period, with ranges of 40 Ma or more:

put <- function(i, truth, ...) {
  v <- list(...)
  for (nm in names(v)) fos[i, nm] <<- v[[nm]]
  fos$truth[i] <<- truth
}
i <- sample(n, 140)
put(i[1:20], "centroid", lng = rep(c(-112.4962, 103.0563, 10.3815), length.out = 20),
    lat = rep(c(45.6881, 46.8258, 51.1064), length.out = 20), cc = rep(c("US", "MN", "DE"), length.out = 20))
put(i[21:35], "museum", lng = rep(c(8.6517, -0.1764), length.out = 15),
    lat = rep(c(50.1175, 51.4958), length.out = 15))
put(i[36:45], "zero", lng = 0, lat = 0)
put(i[46:70], "age_copied", max_ma = fos$min_ma[i[46:70]])
put(i[71:90], "age_swapped", min_ma = fos$max_ma[i[71:90]], max_ma = fos$min_ma[i[71:90]])
put(i[91:130], "age_period", min_ma = 23, max_ma = sample(c(66, 145), 40, TRUE))
put(i[131:140], "centroid_near", lng = -112.4962, lat = 45.6881 + 0.027, cc = "US")
table(fos$truth)
#> 
#>    age_copied    age_period   age_swapped      centroid centroid_near 
#>            25            40            20            20            10 
#>         clean        museum          zero 
#>          1360            15            10

Flagging

occ_columns() maps the PBDB names onto the fields the tests read. The tests are the record tests of CoordinateCleaner’s clean_fossils(), whose defaults are agesequal, centroids, equal, gbif, institutions, validity and zeros plus two outlier tests (spatiotemp, temprange) that the section on outliers below adds; here age_equal is its agesequal, and the country check runs too because the table has country codes:

cols <- occ_columns(lon = "lng", lat = "lat", species = "accepted_name", country = "cc",
                    id = "occurrence_no")
tests <- c("invalid", "zero", "equal", "centroid", "institution", "gbif_headquarters",
           "country_mismatch", "age_equal")
f <- flag_occurrences(fos, tests = tests, columns = cols)

age_equal flags a record whose minimum age is equal to or greater than its maximum age. A zero-length range usually means one age was entered in both fields; an inverted one, that the two were swapped. Either way the age of the record is not usable as it stands. Per error type:

show <- c("zero", "centroid", "institution", "country_mismatch", "age_equal")
tab <- aggregate(as.data.frame(f)[paste0("flag_", show)], by = list(truth = f$truth), FUN = sum)
names(tab) <- c("truth", show)
knitr::kable(tab)
truth zero centroid institution country_mismatch age_equal
age_copied 0 0 0 0 25
age_period 0 0 0 0 0
age_swapped 0 0 0 0 20
centroid 0 20 0 0 0
centroid_near 0 0 0 0 0
clean 0 0 0 10 0
museum 0 7 15 13 0
zero 10 0 0 10 0

The 45 copied or swapped ages are all caught by age_equal, and only by it. The period-dated records are not: a range from 23 to 66 Ma is wide, but valid. The zero coordinates also fail country_mismatch, since (0, 0) is in the Gulf of Guinea. The museum records kept the country code of their locality, so most of them also fail country_mismatch; the 7 at the London museum also lie within 1 km of the admin-1 label point of Kensington and Chelsea. The 10 clean records flagged by country_mismatch are real border cases: the German box reaches east into Czechia and, once, west into France. The 10 collections placed about 3 km from the centroid of the United States are not flagged at the default 1 km.

Buffers for fossil data

clean_fossils() uses wider buffers than clean_coordinates(), given in degrees: centroids_rad = 0.05 and inst_rad = 0.001, about 5.6 km and 111 m of latitude. Fossil localities are often georeferenced coarsely, so a centroid buffer of a few kilometres catches collections placed near a centroid rather than on it. The buffers here are in metres:

f5 <- flag_occurrences(fos, tests = tests, columns = cols,
                       buffers = list(centroid = 5600, institution = 111))
c(centroid_1km = sum(f$flag_centroid), centroid_5.6km = sum(f5$flag_centroid))
#>   centroid_1km centroid_5.6km 
#>             27             37

The wider buffer adds 10 records:

table(f$truth[f5$flag_centroid & !f$flag_centroid])
#> 
#> centroid_near 
#>            10

Clean records that happen to lie within 5.6 km of a centroid would be added too, so a wider buffer trades coarse georeferences caught against clean records lost; the per-test tally of the clean subset shows that cost on real data.

The width of the age range

CoordinateCleaner’s cf_range() with method = "time" flags records whose range is wider than max_range Ma. That is a threshold on a numeric field, so here it stays a raw column and is cut when tallying, which lets one flag pass serve any threshold:

f$age_range <- f$max_ma - f$min_ma
t <- tally_flags(f, bins = list(age_range = c(5, 15, 40)),
                 rules = list(coords = c("zero", "centroid", "institution", "country_mismatch"),
                              ages = "age_equal"))
knitr::kable(t[, c("age_range_bin", "n", "removed_coords", "removed_ages")])
age_range_bin n removed_coords removed_ages
<5 545 22 45
5-15 915 33 0
>=40 40 0 0

The 45 records with a zero or negative range fall into the lowest bin, where age_equal removes them; the 40 period-dated records form the top bin. The distribution shows where a cut would fall:

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(as.data.frame(f), aes(age_range)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, boundary = 0, fill = "#2C5D73") +
  labs(x = "age range (Ma)", y = "records") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA))

A cleaned table for a study at stage resolution then combines the rule with a cut on the raw column:

keep <- !has_flag(f$flags, tests) & f$age_range <= 15
table(f$truth[keep])
#> 
#> centroid_near         clean 
#>            10          1350

Outliers within a taxon

Three tests compare a record with the other records of its taxon, here the genus in accepted_name. age_range_outlier flags age ranges far wider than the taxon’s others, the temprange test of clean_fossils(). age_outlier flags ages far from the taxon’s others, and spatiotemporal_outlier records far from the others in space and time together, the spatiotemp test. The last two draw an age from each record’s range, repeat the test five times and keep the majority; the draws are seeded per taxon, so the flags are the same on every run:

otests <- c("age_range_outlier", "age_outlier", "spatiotemporal_outlier")
g <- flag_occurrences(fos, tests = otests, columns = cols)
tab <- aggregate(as.data.frame(g)[paste0("flag_", otests)], by = list(truth = g$truth), FUN = sum)
names(tab) <- c("truth", otests)
knitr::kable(tab)
truth age_range_outlier age_outlier spatiotemporal_outlier
age_copied 0 0 0
age_period 40 8 3
age_swapped 0 0 0
centroid 0 0 0
centroid_near 0 0 0
clean 0 0 0
museum 0 0 0
zero 0 0 0

age_range_outlier flags all 40 period-dated records and no other. The two tests that draw ages flag fewer of them: an age drawn from 23 to 66 or 145 Ma lands among the genus’s ages of 23 to 72 Ma in many draws, so age_outlier flags 8 of the 40 and spatiotemporal_outlier 3. None of the three flags a clean record. The museum records are not outliers in space here, because every genus in the simulated table occurs in all three regions.

The options are set per test through settings, with CoordinateCleaner’s defaults: method ("quantile" or "mad"), mltpl (5), size_thresh (7 records per taxon), replicates (5) and seed. A stricter fence for the range test and a different seed for the draws:

g2 <- flag_occurrences(fos, tests = otests, columns = cols,
                       settings = list(age_range_outlier = list(mltpl = 2),
                                       age_outlier = list(seed = 7)))
colSums(as.data.frame(g2)[paste0("flag_", otests)])
#>      flag_age_range_outlier            flag_age_outlier 
#>                          40                          10 
#> flag_spatiotemporal_outlier 
#>                           3

The range test flags the same 40 records with the stricter fence, since their ranges are many times wider than the genus’s others. Another seed gives other draws: with seed 7, age_outlier flags 10 of the period-dated records instead of 8.

Comparison with CoordinateCleaner

age_equal and cf_equal() give identical flags:

theirs <- !CoordinateCleaner::cf_equal(fos, value = "flagged", verbose = FALSE)
identical(f$flag_age_equal, theirs)
#> [1] TRUE

The outlier tests above are compared with cf_age(), cf_outl() and cf_range() in the package’s test suite: age_range_outlier gives identical flags, and the two tests that draw ages give identical flags when no age has to be drawn.

Fossils in GBIF data

GBIF holds fossil specimens alongside modern records, marked by basisOfRecord = "FOSSIL_SPECIMEN", usually without PBDB-style age fields. basis_fossil flags them, so a study of living distributions drops them and a palaeontological one keeps only them:

g <- data.frame(basisOfRecord = c("HUMAN_OBSERVATION", "FOSSIL_SPECIMEN", "PRESERVED_SPECIMEN"),
                decimalLongitude = c(16.37, 11.2, 14.5), decimalLatitude = c(48.21, 50.1, 47.1))
flag_occurrences(g, tests = c("invalid", "basis_fossil"))$flag_basis_fossil
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE
